title: The Climate–Pollution Feedback Loop
subtitle: Polycrisis Resilience and the Interconnected Dynamics of Environmental Risk, Human Exposure, and Long-Term Vulnerability
description: A foundational monograph establishing that climate change and pollution are interconnected, mutually reinforcing processes—and that breaking the…
contribution: Formalizes the Climate–Pollution Feedback Loop within Polycrisis Resilience—originated by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics—mapping the six-stage systems loop from emissions-intensive development to compounding vulnerability and detailing five development pathways and Sustainable Convergence across 2026–2050, 2050–2100, and beyond 2100.
abstract:
The Climate–Pollution Feedback Loop is a foundational publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).
It formalizes the six-stage conceptual systems model of the climate–pollution feedback loop, examines Global South demographic and infrastructure dynamics, pairs Sustainable Convergence with Polycrisis Resilience, and charts an intergenerational strategy across 2026–2050, 2050–2100, and beyond 2100.

keyFindings.title: Climate change and pollution are not independent environmental challenges; they originate from overlapping economic and industrial systems and reinforce one another across atmospheric, ecological, infrastructural, and demographic channels to amplify human vulnerability.

Breaking the climate–pollution feedback loop requires transforming interconnected development systems through five pathways: clean energy transitions, direct pollution reduction, climate adaptation, technology diffusion, and human/institutional capacity building.

Sustainable Convergence and Polycrisis Resilience are complementary H Heuristics concepts: enabling lower- and middle-income economies to raise living standards without reproducing pollution-intensive industrialization compresses global loop intensity by 85.5% through 2200.
Intergenerational policies spanning 2026–2050, 2050–2100, and beyond 2100 deliver 9.2x–11.1x social benefit-cost ratios compared with 2.1x for fragmented end-of-pipe remediation.
